r3-zipkin-09.query: An HTTP span upload is acknowledged as accepted, but the storage write fails afterwards. How is that loss counted, and which server endpoint reports that count in its JSON metrics document?
expectedFacts: Collector.accept schedules StoreSpans on the executor and calls the caller's callback onSuccess right after scheduling, before storage is attempted, so the upload is acknowledged regardless of the later storage outcome.
When storage fails, StoreSpans.onError calls handleStorageError, which calls metrics.incrementSpansDropped(spans.size()) and logs only at debug level.
MicrometerCollectorMetrics increments the counter zipkin_collector.spans_dropped tagged with the transport (http for HTTP uploads).
ZipkinMetricsController serves /metrics and writes each zipkin_collector counter as counter.<name>.<transport>, so the loss appears as counter.zipkin_collector.spans_dropped.http.
Endpoint.Builder.serviceName lowercases service names (Locale.ROOT) when a reported span's endpoint is built, so stored service names are always lowercase.
QueryRequest.Builder.build lowercases the query's serviceName, remoteServiceName and spanName, and treats an empty name (or the span name "all") as unset.

Apart from the debug flag, the decision depends only on the trace ID and the configured rate: the lower 64 bits of the trace ID are parsed and their absolute value is compared with a boundary derived from the rate, so instances with the same rate reach the same answer for the same trace.
Debug spans always pass the sampler.
The boundary is (long)(Long.MAX_VALUE * rate); Long.MIN_VALUE is mapped to Long.MAX_VALUE to avoid always dropping.
A call is an error when the span's tags contain the key "error" (any value).

When a span has no error tag and its nearest remote ancestor is a client span whose id equals the span's parent id (an RPC split into a client span and a child server span), the client ancestor's error tag decides whether the call counts as an error.
addLink increments a per-(parent, child) call count and, for errors, a separate error count.

validateAndStoreSpans calls testForUnexpectedFormat(decoder, body) before handing the bytes to the collector; for the v2 JSON decoder it looks for the byte sequence ending in yAnnotations" (binaryAnnotations) and reports JSON_V1.
On a mismatch it fails the request with an IllegalArgumentException (Expected a JSON_V2 encoded list, but received: JSON_V1) and does not pass the body to the collector.

r3-zipkin-22.query: Which check refuses a Cassandra cluster in which some node runs a release older than the minimum supported one, and does that check always run?

expectedFacts: doAccept computes how many spans must be recovered (current + incoming - maxSpanCount) and calls evictToRecoverSpans before adding the new spans.

deleteOldestTrace removes the trace whose timestamp key is last in the descending-by-timestamp map, i.e. the oldest, including all its spans; evictToRecoverSpans repeats this until enough spans are recovered.
When search is enabled, services no longer referenced by any remaining trace also have their span-name and remote-service-name entries removed.

The repository has only head-style sampling: CollectorSampler decides per span from the trace ID alone (lower 64 bits compared with a rate boundary; debug spans always kept), applied in Collector.sample before storage.
Nothing buffers a trace until complete before deciding; self-tracing uses Brave samplers for the server's own requests.
There is no error-aware or latency-aware keep/drop policy anywhere in the server, collectors or storage.
